fullPassage:
Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) special=특별한 / ordinary=평범한 (B) featuring=특별히 포함하는 / excluding=제외하는 (C) announce=발표하다 / cancel=취소하다
det.analysis:
① ordinary — featuring — announce: (A) 우승자에게 주는 상은 '평범한'이 아니라 '특별한'(special) 투어
② special — excluding — cancel: (B) 사진 촬영은 우승자와 반 친구를 '제외'가 아니라 '특별히 포함'(featuring) (C) 우승자를 '취소'가 아니라 '발표'
③ special — featuring — announce: '특별한' 투어 상, 우승자를 '포함'한 촬영, 우승자 '발표' ←정답
④ ordinary — excluding — cancel: (A)(B)(C) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: '특별한'(special) 상, 우승자를 '포함'(featuring)한 촬영, 우승자 '발표'(announce)로 이어지는 흐름

det.korean: (A) tall=높은 / short=낮은 (B) high=높이 / low=낮게 (C) narrower=더 좁은 / wider=더 넓은

④ lose: 환자들이 최대한 많이 '잃으려는(lose)' 욕구? 환자는 최대한 많이 '소유(own)'하려 함 ←정답
det.tip: 저장 강박 환자는 물건을 own(소유)하려 함. lose(잃다)는 정반대

questions.passage: Have you ever seen rows of ①<u>identical</u> fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being ②<u>wasted</u>. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as ③<u>bad</u> as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps ④<u>protect</u> the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① identical=똑같은 ② wasted=낭비되는 ③ good→bad (부적절) ④ protect=보호하다
det.analysis:
① identical: 진열대에 줄지어 놓인 '똑같은' 과일 — 적절
② wasted: 멀쩡한 농산물이 '낭비되고' 있음 — 적절
③ bad: 낭비된 농산물이 마트 것만큼 '나쁜' 맛? 맛은 똑같이 '좋다(good)'가 원문이라 부적절 ←정답
④ protect: 환경을 '보호'하는 데 도움 — 적절
det.tip: 낭비된 농산물도 맛은 마트 것만큼 좋다(good). bad(나쁜)는 정반대

questions.passage: Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a (A)[identical / unique] form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it (B)[compares / ignores] the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is (C)[deleted / added] to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) unique=고유한 / identical=똑같은 (B) compares=비교하다 / ignores=무시하다 (C) added=추가된 / deleted=삭제된
det.analysis:
(A) 손바닥을 신원 확인의 '고유한(unique)' 수단으로 쓴다는 흐름 — identical(똑같은)은 부적절
(B) 일치를 찾으려면 패턴을 기존 스캔과 '비교(compares)'해야 함 — ignores(무시)는 반대
(C) 일치가 없으면 데이터베이스에 '추가된다(added)' — deleted(삭제)는 반대
③ unique — compares — added ←정답
det.tip: unique(고유한) → compares(비교) → added(추가)

questions.passage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ①<u>ideal</u> as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would ②<u>spread</u> around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by ③<u>melting</u> sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more ④<u>rare</u> tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① ideal=이상적인 ② spread=퍼지다 ③ melting=녹이는 ④ frequent→rare (부적절)
det.analysis:
① ideal: 사하라만큼 이상적인 곳이 없음 — 적절
② spread: 온난화가 지구로 퍼짐 — 적절
③ melting: 해빙을 녹여 지구온난화를 가속 — 적절
④ rare: 기온 상승이 '더 드문(rare)' 열대성 저기압을 유발? 문제를 '더' 일으키는 흐름이므로 '더 잦은(frequent)'이 맞아 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 기온 상승 → 더 frequent(잦은) 저기압. rare(드문)는 반대

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an (A)[conscious / unconscious] bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is (B)[prized / ignored], such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively (C)[many / few] women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) unconscious=무의식적인 / conscious=의식적인 (B) prized=소중히 여겨지는 / ignored=무시되는 (C) few=(수가) 적은 / many=많은
det.analysis:
① conscious—prized—few: (A) 전 세계에서 일어나는 '무의식적인(unconscious)' 편견이라 unconscious가 맞음
② unconscious—prized—few: 무의식적 편견 + 지능이 '소중히 여겨지는(prized)' 분야 + 여성이 '적은(few)' 분야 ←정답
③ unconscious—ignored—many: (B)(C) 지능이 '소중히 여겨지고(prized)', 여성이 '적은(few)' 분야임
④ conscious—prized—many: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: unconscious(무의식적) 편견, prized(소중히 여겨지는) 지능, few(적은) 여성

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has <u>devised</u> an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 devised와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: devised=고안했다 / created=만들어냈다 / canceled=취소했다 / followed=따랐다 / delayed=미뤘다
det.analysis:
① created: 만들어냈다 — devised의 동의어 ←정답
② canceled: 취소했다 — 의미 반대
③ followed: 따랐다 — 의미 다름
④ delayed: 미뤘다 — 의미 다름
det.tip: 특이한 계획을 devised(고안했다) = created(만들어냈다)

questions.passage: Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The ①<u>theme</u> of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about ②<u>hiding</u> community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot ③<u>featuring</u> the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to ④<u>announce</u> a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① theme=주제 ② hiding=숨기는 것 → showcasing(보여주는 것) ③ featuring=특별히 포함하는 ④ announce=발표하다
det.analysis:
① theme: 포스터의 '주제'는 '공동체 통합' — 적절
② hiding: 경쟁보다 공동체 정신을 '보여주는'(showcasing) 행사인데 '숨기는'(hiding) 것은 모순 ←정답
③ featuring: 우승자와 반 친구들을 '특별히 포함'한 사진 촬영 — 적절
④ announce: 우승자를 '발표'하려는 흐름 — 적절
det.tip: 경쟁보다 공동체 정신을 '보여주는'(showcasing) 행사. hiding(숨기는)은 정반대

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the __________ it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: slower=더 느린 / heavier=더 무거운 / faster=더 빠른 / weaker=더 약한
det.analysis:
① slower: 더 느리다? 좁을수록 빨라진다는 강물 비유와 반대
② heavier: 더 무겁다? 무게 이야기가 아님
③ faster: 강물처럼 통로가 좁을수록 바람이 '더 빠르게' 움직임 ←정답
④ weaker: 더 약하다? 좁을수록 세진다는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: 물이 흐르는 강 비유 → 좁을수록(the narrower) 더 빠르게(faster) 움직임

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be <u>required</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 required와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:

② ignored: 무시된 — 의미 다름
③ reduced: 줄어든 — 의미 다름
④ needed: 필요한 — required의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: additional methods may be required(필요한) = needed(필요한)

So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than <u>normal</u>. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 normal과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: normal=보통의 / usual=평상시의 / strange=이상한 / illegal=불법의 / final=마지막의
det.analysis:
① usual: 평상시의 — normal(보통의)의 동의어 ←정답
② strange: 이상한 — normal과 반대
③ illegal: 불법의 — 의미 다름
